claims.text: No published information on soy sauce type used. At this style of Japanese omakase, wheat-containing soy sauce is standard unless a chef explicitly uses tamari or GF alternatives — none mentioned anywhere.
No allergy handling policy is publicly documented. Given the referral-only, single-party-per-night format, dietary needs would need to be communicated through the introducer at the time of booking.

One chef, one small party per night — if dietary needs are communicated in advance through an introducer, the format theoretically allows for fully customised preparation. No shared fryer risk from other tables.
Tempura is on the menu, meaning wheat flour is actively used in the kitchen. No source mentions a dedicated fryer or separate prep area for allergen-sensitive orders.
No source confirms wheat-free soy sauce. Standard Japanese tsuyu (the dipping/broth base for soba) contains wheat-based soy sauce; this shop has given no indication it deviates from that norm.
Fish-based dashi is implied by the classic broth flavor described by reviewers; pork and chicken bowls are also served, making a fully plant-based meal extremely unlikely.
No allergy-handling information appears in any reviewed source. With no English menu and a small cash-only operation, allergy communication will require Japanese or a translation aid.
Soba noodles are buckwheat-based, which is inherently gluten-free before any broth or coating is applied — a useful starting point for a conversation with staff.

name: 創作串揚げ つだ 金シャチ横丁店 (Sosaku Kushiage Tsuda Kinshachi Yokocho)

claims.text: All kushiage items share the same lard-and-vegetable-oil frying blend; there is no separate dedicated GF fryer. Wheat from standard batter will be present in the oil throughout service.

The house dipping options include a blended soy sauce (合わせ醤油, described as 30+ ingredient base) which in standard Japanese practice contains wheat. Salt, sansho salt, lemon, and mustard options exist and are likely wheat-free, but confirmation is required.
All skewers are fried in the same shared oil (lard-and-vegetable blend). Lard is animal-derived. Even vegetable skewers are cooked in lard-containing oil alongside meat and seafood items.

Hitosara lists フードアレルギー対応可 (food-allergy accommodation available) for this location. The nature and extent of accommodation is not further specified; direct inquiry before visiting is strongly recommended.
The restaurant uses exclusively domestic, sushi-grade ingredients and communicates openly about provenance — the counter format allows direct conversation with the chef about what is in each skewer.
This is a pasta-specialist kitchen; wheat flour is the primary ingredient in virtually every dish. Cross-contamination risk for celiac diners is high and has not been addressed in any public source.
Pasta sets include soup, bread (focaccia), and quiche, all of which likely contain dairy or egg. No plant-based alternatives have been noted in any review or listing.
Naan (wheat flour) is baked in the tandoor oven and served as a core item; the same tandoor is used for marinated meats such as lamb seekh kebab, meaning shared cooking surfaces are in active use.
No confirmation that gluten-free tamari or alternative soy sauce is used. Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is the default in this style of fusion spice cooking.

Fish sauce (魚醤) is used directly in at least one appetizer preparation (mint sauce and fish sauce namero); meat and seafood are cooked throughout the small kitchen, making vegan cross-contact highly probable.
No information on staff allergy training or allergen labeling has been found in any source. Reservations are handled via Instagram DM, which could provide a channel to raise dietary needs in advance.
Small 15-seat independent kitchen means a single team handles all cooking, reducing the complexity of communicating dietary needs — direct conversation with the chef-owner is feasible.

name: スパイシーカレー クスクス 白壁店 (Spicy Curry Kusukusu Shirakabe)

claims.text: Naan (wheat) is baked on-premises and is the default bread; the kitchen handles wheat continuously. No dedicated GF prep area or protocol is documented.

Indian-Nepalese curry cuisine does not typically use soy sauce; no soy sauce is mentioned in any source reviewed. However, no allergen statement has been published by the restaurant, so this cannot be guaranteed.

Ghee, yogurt, and cream are standard in multiple menu items (Malai Tikka, butter-based preparations). A shared kitchen serving meat and dairy means cross-contact for vegan diners is probable without explicit accommodation.

No allergy-handling policy or allergen menu has been published. Phone reservations are noted as unavailable (online booking only), making pre-visit allergy communication more difficult — diners should plan to ask at the counter on arrival.
Basmati rice is available as a wheat-free alternative to naan and can be ordered as part of the set meal, offering a naturally gluten-free carb base.

name: 炭火やきとり ごまめ泉 (Sumibiyakitori Gomame Izumi)

claims.text: No information on shared grilling surfaces or kitchen cross-contamination practices. The charcoal grill is almost certainly shared across all skewer types.
Tare (yakitori dipping sauce) is standard in Japanese yakitori and typically contains wheat-based soy sauce. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative has been mentioned by any source.
All cooking surfaces are used exclusively for meat and seafood; there is no plant-based section and no vegan cross-contact protocol documented.

No allergy menu, allergy declaration, or staff allergy-handling procedure has been documented by any source checked. Phone inquiry (052-212-5595) before visiting is strongly advised for any dietary restriction.
Shio (salt) grilled skewers avoid tare entirely and may be the safest ordering path for wheat-avoiders, though shared-grill cross-contamination remains unconfirmed.

name: 鮨 極 はなれ (Sushi Kiwami Hanare)

claims.text: No information on cross-contamination controls is published. Shared prep surfaces and utensils in a small sushi counter are a realistic concern for celiac guests.
Edomae nigiri is traditionally brushed or served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. No tamari or wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned on any platform.
Seafood, fish, tamagoyaki, and eel are the entirety of the menu; no plant-based items or vegan accommodations exist.
No allergy menu, gluten-free policy, or allergen labelling is documented on Tabelog, Gnavi, HotPepper, or the parent brand website. Guests with dietary restrictions should call ahead.
The shari (sushi rice) is made with red vinegar and plain rice — both inherently gluten-free ingredients — so the rice base itself poses no gluten risk absent cross-contamination.
